title: Contest verdicts that depend on load
description: Your judge starts a new Docker container for each test case and enforces a 2-second wall-clock limit per test. During a contest burst, workers run 3 containers per core. Users report that identical correct solutions get Accepted in practice but Time Limit Exceeded in the contest, and verdicts take 30+ seconds. What change best addresses both problems?

options.text: Double every time limit during contests
options.explanation: It hides some false TLEs but keeps verdicts load-dependent and unfair, lets genuinely slow solutions pass, and does nothing about container startup latency.

options.text: Run tests directly on the worker host without containers to remove startup overhead
options.explanation: It fixes latency by abandoning isolation, which is unacceptable for untrusted code.

options.text: Run all tests of a submission in one sandbox via an in-sandbox harness, measure each test by CPU time with a wall-clock guard, and stop oversubscribing cores (pre-scale for the contest instead)
options.explanation: One sandbox removes per-test startup cost, CPU-time limits make verdicts independent of host load, the wall-clock guard still catches sleeping programs, and dedicated capacity keeps runtimes reproducible.

options.text: Return Accepted immediately and judge in the background, revising the verdict later
options.explanation: Provisional verdicts break contest scoring and user trust, and the underlying unfairness remains.
